key_insight: A two-stage machine-learning workflow—broad pretraining plus targeted fine-tuning—can capture how amino-silane passivants interact with hybrid halide perovskite surfaces as coverage increases.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to design and optimize molecular surface passivation strategies that may improve defect control and optoelectronic performance in perovskite solar cells.
method: Built a large open training set, hyP-26, covering diverse metal and hybrid halide perovskite structures.
Fine-tuned the model on a small, specialized dataset for an amino-silane passivating molecule on perovskite surfaces.
Used the trained potential to simulate mixed-composition perovskite surfaces across varying molecular coverages.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a curated large dataset plus a small specialized passivation dataset and evaluates the approach by observing coverage-dependent interaction trends at the surface.
watch_item: The workflow depends on high-quality specialized fine-tuning data, so transfer to other passivants or surface chemistries may require new reference calculations.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
